thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming-tail p99 breach for eu-west2 (service=streaming-api). Observed p99 ~= 1.4s, error spikes (TLS handshake failures). Pager: @sarah. See runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail-latency

sarah: ack - I'm on it. seeing elevated TLS handshake durations in traces (handshake_slow_count up). Tagging @ken for network correlation. Starting trace aggregation now.

ken: digging into VPC egress metrics for eu-west2c — seeing a sharp increase in retransmits and SYN retries originating from hosts in azc -> NAT gateway 3. Possible ephemeral port exhaustion or NAT overload. Confirming conntrack states.

mike: metrics snapshot: p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 1450ms, error-rate ~ 0.9%. Streaming stalls (tail) correlate with handshake timeouts in the logs. Quick log snippet: ```
2024-04-11T14:12:03Z service=streaming request_id=rx-9f2 stall_ms=1492 stage=tls_handshake peer=34.120.54.12
2024-04-11T14:12:05Z service=streaming request_id=rx-9f3 err=handshake_timeout
```

jess: are we seeing DNS failures too? earlier incidents had DNS backoff -> handshake spikes. If DNS is slow, TLS attempts pile up. @mike can you grep for NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL around the spike window?

mike: quick grep shows increased DNS retries from streaming hosts (~3x baseline). Example: ```
resolver=10.0.1.10 query=api.external-ml.net resp=SERVFAIL
resolver=10.0.1.10 query=api.external-ml.net retry=1
```
But the bulk of TLS failures are SYN/RTOs. leaning NAT/egress path.

ken: confirmed conntrack high-water in eu-west2c on NAT nodes: ```
# conntrack -S
entries: 65536 (limit 65536)
seen_established: 58234
```
We hit conntrack limit -> aggressive TIME_WAIT accumulation. Also seeing ephemeral port exhaustion pattern (many CLOSE_WAIT to external IPs).

infra-bot: temporary mitigation options from playbook: 1) scale NAT gateway pool + add egress nodes, 2) route a portion of traffic to eu-west2a/b, 3) apply short-term iptables cleanup to reduce TIME_WAIT. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/vpc-egress-handoff

sarah: let's do 1) + 2) in parallel. @mike start scaling NAT nodes in azc, @jess prepare traffic router policy to shift 30% traffic to azb/aza. I'll coordinate customer comms.

mike: scaling NAT pool +2 in eu-west2c now. Commands I ran: ```
./infra scale-nat --region eu-west2 --az c --count +2 --reason "incident 1723456789"
# system checks
NAT_NODE_OK=2/2
```
Observed ephemeral port free-up starting ~30s after node join. Monitoring conntrack.

jess: applied traffic router policy: weight(eu-west2c)=0.7, weight(eu-west2b)=0.2, weight(eu-west2a)=0.1. Command: ```
/trafficctl set-weights streaming-api eu-west2 0.7,0.2,0.1
```
Routing change propagated to edge in ~45s.

elaine: customer-impact summary for statuspage draft: "A subset of streaming sessions in eu-west2 experienced higher-than-normal latency and reconnects between 14:12-14:18 UTC due to egress infrastructure contention. Mitigations in progress; some users may have seen stalls up to ~1.5s." Preparing update for CS.

ken: conntrack count dropping after NAT scale: entries: 40234. Also reduced retransmits on azc->internet. TLS handshake success rate climbing.

mike: captured tcpdump from host-02 in eu-west2c showing SYN retransmit pattern before scale: ```
14:12:04.123 IP host-02 > 34.120.54.12: Flags [S], seq 12345
14:12:04.623 IP host-02 > 34.120.54.12: Flags [S], seq 12345 (retrans)
14:12:05.623 IP host-02 > 34.120.54.12: Flags [S], seq 12345 (retrans)
```
After NAT nodes joined, retransmit rate drops markedly.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Temporary mitigations applied (nat_scale, route_shift). p99 trending down toward SLO. Continue monitoring for 30m.

sarah: good. we'll keep this thread for post-incident notes. @samir - you're next on call in 30m; I'm handing off monitoring and follow-ups. Summary for handoff: cause = egress conntrack/ephemeral port exhaustion in eu-west2c causing TLS handshake spikes and streaming tail latency. Mitigations = scaled NAT pool (+2 nodes), shifted 30% traffic to other AZs. Customer comms drafted. Owner for P0 follow-up: @ken (networking) and @mike (infra) to produce root-cause and long-term remediation (conntrack limit increase, NAT autoscale).

samir: ack takeover at 14:40 UTC. I'll watch graphs and ping if anything reoccurs.

sarah: thanks team. I'll file an incident ticket and assign postmortem owners. Will include logs, pcaps, runbook steps, and timing. :white_check_mark:
